resolution.note: backlog triage 2026-11-07: Handoff across Claude/Codex; same outcome

title: Make Herdr session handoff measurable, acknowledged and single-writer for Claude and Codex
body:
Outcome: one handoff mechanism owned in KRN (shared protocol + client adapter + repository adapter) so long work moves between Claude Code and Codex sessions in Herdr without losing goal, grants, evidence or single-writer control. Order: measurement and takeover correctness first, cost tuning second.
Source: operator handoff 2026-11-05, full report /home/krn/reports/Przekazywanie kontekstu w Herdr.md, notes /home/krn/research_notes/Przekazywanie kontekstu w Herdr/.
Confirmed defects (code + controlled repro, no observed data loss yet):
- global context-usage.py takes the last message.usage without provenance: a sidechain record replaced 210k with 11k; synthetic/partial usage gives 0 and should_relay=false. Missing data must be unknown, never 0; post-compaction samples are stale; worker usage never stands in for the main session. Claude occupancy = input + cache_creation + cache_read; Codex cached_input_tokens is a subset of input_tokens (do not add).
- global relay.sh waits a fixed 15 s and reads lifecycle; no proof the successor read the right handoff.
- scripts/claude/successor-launch.ts treats command success as start success and has the successor retire the predecessor before reading the handoff; retirement sweeps marked tabs across the whole workspace without checking project, outcome and unsent input (overlaps t-e6kke4g).
- Codex: no proven Codex->Codex relay; needs its own adapter (session telemetry or App Server thread/tokenUsage/updated), cross-client handoff tested separately (overlaps t-b6v615x, t-tdkpgag).
- Inherited HERDR pane ids can return pane_not_found; never fall back to the focused pane.
Protocol: checkpoint -> freeze predecessor writes -> durable handoff doc -> constrained successor start -> ACK of handoff id + hash -> atomic owner change (write generation) -> successor writes -> careful predecessor close. A timeout never proves a start did not happen: read the record before retrying. Single writer is cooperative until enforcement is found; a new hook needs a separate install/hook-trust grant.
Thresholds: keep 300k as reference; split prepare / no-new-large-work / execute thresholds; 150-180k is a hypothesis for a pilot on identical tasks.
Boundaries: no install/seal, production or hook trust without their grants; never close foreign, working or ambiguous panes; repos may hold others' uncommitted work.
Proof: tests for lost ACK, timeout after real start, two starters, crash before/after owner change, stale write grant, pane change, unsent input, dirty repo, active workers, compaction mid-work, on the real Herdr interface in an isolated workspace.
First slice: fix measurement (provenance, unknown/stale, per-client sum) with Claude receiver proof and an explicit Codex adapter scope; then successor ACK.
